issues.description: Arg name mismatch: parser uses --train-config / max_steps but trainer reads trainer_args["max_step"]
issues.detail: The docstring promises max_steps but __init__ reads trainer_args["max_step"]. Similarly the trainer also reads save_interval/log_interval but never uses log_interval anywhere. A KeyError on the first run is not a hypothetical; this is what "does it run?" catches. Pick one spelling and use it.

issues.description: local_rank defaults to None then is passed to torch.cuda.set_device, which will crash on standalone runs
issues.detail: argparse default is None; deepspeed launchers usually set it via env or --local_rank, but the script unconditionally calls torch.cuda.set_device(args.local_rank). If the launcher passes LOCAL_RANK in env (common with deepspeed/torchrun), this dies immediately. Read int(os.environ.get("LOCAL_RANK", args.local_rank or 0)) and validate.

issues.description: Specifier parsing uses str.split() which silently drops multi-token specifiers and whitespace edge cases
issues.detail: valid-*-specifier is documented as colon-separated like "asr:librispeech:valid.json" but the loop does args.valid_unregistered_specifier.split() with no separator. Multiple specifiers presumably space-separated, but this is never documented and a single empty default "" splits to []. Be explicit: pick a separator, document it, and validate.

issues.description: Checkpoint dir scan blows up on non-step subdirectories
issues.detail: _load_checkpoint filters by "step_" in d.name then sorts on int(x.name.split("step_")[-1]). Any directory named e.g. "step_best" or partially-written "step_1234.tmp" raises ValueError mid-sort and kills resume. Match a strict regex like r"^step_(\d+)$" or skip on parse failure. Resume is exactly the path users hit at 3 AM.

issues.description: valid() all_reduces stats with SUM/world_size, but unevenly-sized validation shards make this a biased mean
issues.detail: Each rank averages its own batches into all_stats then SUM/world_size. If shards have different batch counts (common when world_size doesn't divide the valid set), ranks contribute equal weight to the global mean regardless of sample count. Either pad/truncate to equal shard length or weight by sample count. The number you log is not the number you think.

issues.description: log_interval is configured and parsed but never read; wandb.log fires every step
issues.detail: trainer_args["log_interval"] is stored on self and then never used. Either honor it (only wandb.log every log_interval steps) or delete the knob. Dead config is worse than no config because users assume it works.

review.summary: Two new files, ~500 lines, doing one thing (DeepSpeed training launcher + trainer). Scope is fine, diff is readable, style matches surrounding espnet2 code. But the code shows signs of not having been actually run end-to-end: a max_step vs max_steps key mismatch, local_rank defaulting to None and getting passed straight to torch.cuda.set_device, a checkpoint resume that ValueErrors on any non-numeric step_ directory, and a configured log_interval that's never consulted. The valid() reduction also computes a per-rank-equal mean that lies when shards differ. NEEDS-WORK: fix the run-blockers, prove resume works with a stray directory in checkpoints/, then resubmit.
